# Fundamental Analysis: 4062.T

**Fiscal-period note (read once):** 4062.T reports on a March year-end. The company and the documents label the year ending 31 March 2027 as "FY2026". Throughout this report I use **FY3/27** for that year, **FY3/28** for the year ending March 2028, and so on. H1 FY3/27 = April–September 2026. All figures are JPY; the filing quotes 百万円 (millions) and I convert to JPY bn.

---

## 1. Executive conclusion

- **Fundamental rating: Negative** (valuation-driven, not business-quality-driven). Decision horizon: 3–6 months.
- **Business direction: strongly positive.** 4062.T is the leading supplier of high-end IC package substrates into AI GPU/ASIC, server CPU and switching, in a market management describes as structurally undersupplied through the end of the decade [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call].
- **Earnings direction: positive but decelerating in rate of surprise.** H1 FY3/27 operating profit rose 84.6% YoY to JPY60.1bn on sales of JPY262.5bn (+34.3%) [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.1]. Full-year guidance is [[565.0]] sales / [[133.0]] operating profit / [[89.0]] net profit [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.3].
- **Forecast versus guidance:** no edge in FY3/27 — the model equals guidance because it is built as H1 actual plus H2 guided, with no independent H2 adjustment. In FY3/28 the model is [[180.0]] versus company guidance of JPY165bn, because it reverses roughly JPY10bn of embedded price-decline conservatism and adds a measured Cell 8 ramp net of start-up costs.
- **Forecast versus consensus:** the model's FY3/28 operating profit of [[180.0]] is 5.3% below the Citi-cited consensus of [[190.0]], because it does not extrapolate the full current pricing tailwind and assumes a more back-end-loaded Cell 8 ramp.
- **Cash-flow quality: weak on an underlying basis.** H1 operating cash flow of JPY193.2bn includes a JPY118.8bn increase in customer advances [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.9]. Ex-advances, H1 free cash flow is roughly JPY25bn against capex that management guides to ~JPY200bn in FY3/27, ~JPY350bn in FY3/28 and above JPY400bn thereafter [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call].
- **Balance sheet: strong today, eroding on plan.** Net cash of roughly JPY258bn at 30 September 2026 (cash JPY420.5bn less interest-bearing debt JPY162.1bn) [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.4–5]. On the guided capex path, cumulative free cash flow is likely to consume most of that buffer by FY3/29.
- **Valuation conclusion: unattractive.** At the instructed price of [[JPY 8,045]] the stock trades at [[51.2x]] FY3/27 EPS of [[157.2]] and 38.0x my FY3/28 EPS of [[211.9]]. The price sits **above the top of the model's fair-value band of [[JPY 4,715]]–[[JPY 7,858]]**, and even the model's bull case of [[JPY 7,806]] is 3% below spot.
- **Main catalyst (3–6 months):** a decision and disclosure on Cell 7 / Cell 9 with customer-backed terms, and a possible revision of the FY3/31 (company FY2030) target, both guided to occur by end-FY3/27 (March 2027) [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026].
- **Main risk:** the market is already paying for consensus-plus earnings; a Cell 8 qualification slip, EMIB-T yield disappointment, or a visible third-supplier share narrative would compress a 38x multiple on negative free cash flow.
- **Principal limitation:** no peer multiple set, no full consensus beyond the single Citi-cited FY3/28 operating-profit figure, and no company-disclosed FY3/28 revenue/OP guidance document in the corpus (the FY3/28 plan is known only through broker notes).

---

## 2. Company and earnings structure

4062.T makes money in three reportable segments. H1 FY3/27 segment data [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.12]:

| Segment | H1 FY3/27 sales (JPY bn) | H1 FY3/27 segment profit (JPY bn) | Margin | H1 FY3/26 sales / profit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Electronics (IC package substrates) | 172.5 | 50.0 | 29.0% | 113.5 / 25.4 |
| Ceramics (DPF, EV, graphite) | 46.2 | 5.4 | 11.7% | 39.7 / 3.8 |
| Others | 43.8 | 4.6 | 10.5% | 42.2 / 3.3 |
| **Total** | **262.5** | **60.1** | **22.9%** | **195.5 / 32.6** |

Electronics is 66% of sales and 83% of segment profit. It is the only segment that matters for valuation.

**What drives Electronics revenue and margin:**
1. **Substrate area per package**, not unit volumes. Management estimates AI GPU/ASIC unit volumes grow 1.8x from CY26 to CY30 but required SAP area grows 5.4x; server CPU units grow 1.3x but area 2.5x [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-company-presentation-20261030 p.12]. Larger die sizes (3.5 reticle in CY25 to 9+ by CY30) and layer counts (9-X-9 to 14-X-14) drive the area multiplier [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-company-presentation-20261030 p.14].
2. **Qualified capacity.** Management plans domestic high-end capacity to double from an index of 100 in FY3/27 to 200 by FY3/30, against market area demand of 3.5x — i.e. management expects to *lose* share and still run full [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026].
3. **Pricing.** Management states suppliers currently hold the stronger negotiating position but deliberately models ASP declines in guidance because "it is dangerous to optimistically assume current peak pricing will last forever" [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call].
4. **Mix** toward CPU, switching and EMIB-related products, which management says lifts Electronics margin toward 30% in H2 FY3/27 and ~35% by FY3/31 [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call].

**Customer and geographic concentration:** not disclosed in the corpus. The business is plainly concentrated in a small number of AI accelerator and server CPU customers — management refers to "customer requests" driving specific capacity allocation decisions and to customer-funded prepayments (advances received of JPY199.7bn at 30 September 2026) [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.5]. This is a real concentration risk that the documents do not quantify.

**Capital intensity is the defining financial characteristic.** FY3/27 capex of ~JPY200bn is ~35% of guided sales; FY3/28 ~JPY350bn; FY3/29 and beyond >JPY400bn [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call]. Depreciation is guided at JPY81bn in FY3/27 and JPY90bn in FY3/28, with the main Cell 6/Cell 8 depreciation impact deferred to FY3/28 onward because assets remain in construction in progress [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call]. Construction in progress was JPY126.2bn at 30 September 2026, up from JPY111.8bn [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.4].

---

## 3. Latest results and operating drivers

**Company-confirmed facts (H1 FY3/27, six months to 30 September 2026)** [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.1, p.7]:

| | H1 FY3/27 | H1 FY3/26 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Net sales | 262,546 | 195,485 | +34.3% |
| Gross profit | 97,705 | 67,913 | +43.9% |
| Gross margin | 37.2% | 34.7% | +2.5pp |
| SG&A | 37,589 | 35,340 | +6.4% |
| Operating profit | 60,116 | 32,573 | +84.6% |
| Operating margin | 22.9% | 16.7% | +6.2pp |
| Ordinary profit | 61,009 | 32,305 | +88.9% |
| Profit attributable to owners | 38,574 | 22,069 | +74.8% |
| Basic EPS (post-split) | JPY68.63 | JPY39.52 | +73.7% |

**Decomposition (my calculation from segment data):** of the JPY67.1bn sales increase, Electronics contributed JPY59.0bn, Ceramics JPY6.5bn and Others JPY1.6bn. Of the JPY27.5bn operating-profit increase, Electronics contributed JPY24.6bn, Ceramics JPY1.6bn and Others JPY1.4bn. **Electronics is ~90% of the profit delta.**

**The margin story is operating leverage, not just price.** Gross margin rose 2.5pp while SG&A rose only 6.4% against 34.3% sales growth, so SG&A fell from 18.1% to 14.3% of sales. That is the mechanical source of the 6.2pp operating-margin gain. Management attributes the top line to "favorable pricing and exceptionally strong demand for AI-related products" [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call] — that is management's view, and the segment arithmetic is consistent with it, but the company does not disclose the price/volume split.

**Q2 alone (derived as H1 less Q1):** revenue JPY139.3bn, operating profit JPY33.2bn, net profit JPY20.7bn, operating margin 23.8% — a sequential improvement from Q1's 21.8% [model quarterly build; [[139.3]], [[33.2]], [[20.7]]].

**Items that flatter or distort the numbers:**
- **H1 operating cash flow of JPY193.2bn is not an earnings-quality signal.** It includes a JPY118.8bn increase in advances received [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.9]. Customer prepayments reduce funding and stranded-capacity risk; they are not recurring organic cash generation.
- **H1 extraordinary items were a net JPY1.65bn loss**, including a JPY1.61bn loss on retirement of non-current assets and a JPY0.81bn loss on reduction of non-current assets, partly offset by JPY0.81bn subsidy income [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.7]. Small relative to profit.
- **The FY3/26 base year is not clean.** FY3/26 net profit of [[63.7]] exceeded operating profit of [[62.0]]. The vendor annual cash-flow statement shows a JPY40.3bn gain on investment securities in FY3/26 (vendor data, `get_cashflow`, annual). This means the guided +39.7% net-profit growth for FY3/27 understates the +114.4% operating-profit growth, and FY3/26 EPS of [[112.5]] is not a clean earnings base.
- **Ceramics is deteriorating into H2.** H1 Ceramics profit was JPY5.4bn, but management guides H2 Ceramics operating income to only JPY2.1bn on automotive sluggishness [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call]. That is a ~JPY3.3bn half-on-half decline that Electronics must more than offset.

**Data-quality flags I could not resolve:**
- The JPM section of the broker note states FY3/27 group revenue of "¥665.0bn" against guidance of ¥565bn, and Electronics operating profit of "¥141.0bn" against group operating profit of ¥133.0bn [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026]. Both are internally inconsistent; I have not used JPM's segment figures.
- The presentation states Cell 6 "previously announced: JPY220 billion; newly added: JPY150 billion" [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-company-presentation-20261030 p.13], while the call and JPM describe the JPY151bn as incremental to "¥120.0bn already deployed" [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026]. The incremental amount (JPY151bn) is consistent; the base is not. I use JPY151bn as the incremental figure and flag the base as unresolved.
- The earnings-call document is an **internal note reproducing the call**, not a company-issued transcript, and it contains visible analyst corrections to the audio ("Corrected from the garbled audio transcription…") [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call]. I treat its content as management commentary with that caveat.

---

## 4. Management guidance and expectations

**FY3/27 guidance (company disclosure, revised upward on 29 October 2026)** [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.3]:

| Metric | Guidance | YoY |
|---|---|---|
| Net sales | JPY565.0bn | +35.8% |
| Operating income | JPY133.0bn | +114.4% |
| Ordinary income | JPY134.5bn | +121.1% |
| Net profit | JPY89.0bn | +39.7% |
| EPS (post 1:2 split) | JPY157.17 | — |

Implied H2: sales JPY302.5bn, operating profit JPY72.9bn (24.1% margin), net profit JPY50.4bn (16.7% margin) [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call]. H2 operating profit therefore needs to be 1.21x H1 and +148% YoY against a depressed H2 FY3/26 base of JPY29.4bn.

**Medium-term plan (company disclosure, via broker notes):**
- **FY3/28:** revenue JPY650bn, operating profit raised from JPY150bn to **JPY165bn**; Electronics operating profit ~JPY144bn at ~31% margin [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026; doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call]. JPM records the figure as JPY163bn — a minor conflict I cannot resolve [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026].
- **FY3/31 (company FY2030):** JPY1tn sales, JPY300bn+ operating profit, unchanged. Electronics JPY800bn revenue / JPY280bn operating profit [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026].
- **Explicitly excluded from the FY3/31 target:** the new JPY151bn Cell 6 investment, the unused Cell 8 space, and Cell 7/Cell 9 [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026].

**Key assumptions embedded in guidance:**
1. **Deliberate ASP declines.** GS estimates the embedded price-decline assumption is worth ~JPY10bn of FY3/28 operating-profit drag [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026]. Management confirmed it models conservative ASPs for FY3/27–FY3/31 [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call].
2. **Capacity, not demand, is the constraint.** Management expects supply-demand to stay extremely tight through FY3/30 and states there is "no escape" for either customers or suppliers near term [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call].
3. **Cell 8 ramp is back-end loaded.** Main operational ramp and depreciation fall from FY3/28 onward [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call].

**Available consensus:** only one figure exists in the corpus — Citi-cited FY3/28 operating profit of JPY190bn [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026]. There is **no consensus revenue, net profit or EPS** in the corpus. This is a data gap, not evidence that the market is wrong.

**Market reaction:** the shares fell sharply after the results and briefing, which JPM attributes to the medium-term revision being well below expectations and no Cell 7/Cell 9 announcement [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026]. Broker tone was split: GS and JPM constructive, SMBC and Citi negative on the near-term expectations cycle.

---

## 5. Independent forecast

I adopt the verified model's annual path, with the caveats in Section 7.

| JPY bn | FY3/26A | FY3/27E | FY3/28E | FY3/29E |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | [[416.2]] | [[565.0]] | [[660.0]] | [[780.0]] |
| Operating profit | [[62.0]] | [[133.0]] | [[180.0]] | [[230.0]] |
| Operating margin | [[14.9]]% | [[23.5]]% | [[27.3]]% | [[29.5]]% |
| Net profit | [[63.7]] | [[89.0]] | [[120.0]] | [[153.0]] |
| EPS (JPY) | [[112.5]] | [[157.2]] | [[211.9]] | [[270.2]] |

**Quarterly build, FY3/27** (model): Q1 [[123.2]] revenue / [[26.9]] OP / [[17.9]] net; Q2 [[139.3]] / [[33.2]] / [[20.7]]; Q3 [[145.2]] / [[35.0]] / [[24.2]]; Q4 [[157.3]] / [[37.9]] / [[26.2]].

**Key assumptions and where they come from:**
- **FY3/27 is not an independent forecast.** It is H1 actual plus H2 guidance. There is no forecast edge versus guidance for this year, and I state that plainly rather than manufacture one.
- **H2 phasing (Q3/Q4 48/52 split)** is an assumption based on recent Q4-over-Q3 seasonality, not company disclosure. The internal note's own Q3/Q4 build (JPY149.0bn/JPY36.5bn and JPY164.5bn/JPY41.4bn) is more aggressive than the model's, and its full-year FY3/27 operating profit is JPY138bn versus the model's [[133.0]] [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy2027-results-forecast]. I prefer the model's more conservative phasing because the internal note's Q4 revenue step of +10% QoQ is not supported by any disclosed order or qualification milestone.
- **FY3/28 revenue of [[660.0]]** is 1.5% above company guidance of JPY650bn, built from +JPY50bn Cell 8 AI GPU ramp, +JPY30bn advanced-substrate area and mix, +JPY10bn server CPU/EMIB/switch mix, +JPY5bn Ceramics and Other. All four are analyst assumptions; the Cell 8 timing is supported by management's "sequential operation from FY2027" statement [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-company-presentation-20261030 p.13].
- **FY3/28 operating profit of [[180.0]]** = [[133.0]] + [[35]] volume/mix + [[10]] price-decline buffer reversal − [[8]] Cell 8 depreciation and start-up + [[10]] productivity. The buffer reversal is derived from the GS estimate of ~JPY10bn embedded price-decline drag [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026].
- **Tax rate of [[34.0]]%** is consistent with the H1 effective rate of 34.5% (income taxes JPY20,490m on pre-tax profit JPY59,358m) [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.7].
- **FY3/29 is not a company target.** It is interpolated toward the FY3/31 ambition and excludes Cell 6, which starts operation in company FY2029 (FY3/30) [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-company-presentation-20261030 p.13].

**Where I would put ranges rather than points:** FY3/28 operating profit is genuinely a JPY165–190bn range (company guidance to consensus), and I would not defend [[180.0]] to better than ±JPY10bn. FY3/29 is a JPY210–250bn range.

---

## 6. Forecast bridges

**Revenue, FY3/26 → FY3/27 (base [[416.2]]):** +[[67]] H1 actual uplift (H1 FY3/27 net sales JPY262.5bn less H1 FY3/26 JPY195.5bn) and +[[81.8]] H2 guided uplift (H2 guidance JPY302.5bn less prior H2 JPY220.7bn) = [[565.0]]. This is arithmetic, not a driver decomposition: the company does not disclose the price/volume split, so I cannot separate volume from price within the JPY67bn H1 uplift. **Unexplained reconciliation residual: none, but the driver attribution is unavailable.**

**Operating profit, FY3/26 → FY3/27 (base [[62.0]]):** +[[27.5]] H1 actual uplift (JPY60.1bn less JPY32.6bn) and +[[43.5]] H2 guided uplift (H2 guidance JPY72.9bn less prior H2 JPY29.4bn) = [[133.0]]. The H2 uplift is 1.6x the H1 uplift — **this is the single most demanding assumption in the FY3/27 forecast** and it is management's number, not mine.

**Operating profit, FY3/27 → FY3/28 (base [[133.0]]):** +[[35]] higher advanced-substrate volume and mix; +[[10]] price-decline buffer reversal; −[[8]] Cell 8 ramp depreciation and start-up; +[[10]] cost productivity = [[180.0]]. The +[[35]] is an assumption with no disclosed volume or price support; it implies an incremental operating margin of 37% on the JPY95bn revenue increase, which is high but consistent with the H1 FY3/27 incremental margin (JPY27.5bn on JPY67.1bn = 41%). I regard the incremental margin as defensible; the *revenue* increment is the weaker link.

**Net profit, FY3/27 → FY3/28 (base [[89.0]]):** +[[31]] operating-profit growth net of 34% tax = [[120.0]]. This assumes no change in non-operating items, minority interests or the effective tax rate. That is a simplification: H1 FY3/27 non-operating income was +JPY0.9bn and minorities were −JPY0.3bn [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.7]. The conversion is transparent but not independently verified.

**Not bridged:** currency. The corpus does not disclose the assumed FX rate or a yen sensitivity. The internal note states its FY3/28 assumption is ¥145/US$ and that a materially stronger yen is a risk, but provides no quantifiable sensitivity [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy2027-results-forecast]. I therefore cannot decompose the forecast into FX and operations, and I do not pretend to.

---

## 7. Consensus and variant perception

**Where the forecast differs:**

| Metric | Period | Company | Consensus | Model | My view |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Operating profit | FY3/27 | JPY133.0bn | n/a | [[133.0]] | No edge — model = guidance |
| Operating profit | FY3/28 | JPY165.0bn | [[190.0]] | [[180.0]] | Model sits between; ±JPY10bn range |
| Revenue | FY3/28 | JPY650bn | n/a | [[660.0]] | 1.5% above company |

**Why the model differs from guidance (FY3/28):** it reverses ~JPY10bn of embedded price-decline conservatism and adds a measured Cell 8 ramp net of start-up costs, which management's JPY165bn does not fully reflect.

**Why the model differs from consensus (FY3/28):** it does not extrapolate the full current pricing tailwind and assumes a more back-end-loaded Cell 8 ramp than the JPY190bn consensus implies.

**Is there a genuine edge?** For FY3/27, no: "The base case does not currently provide a material forecast edge versus the available consensus for this metric" — and in fact there is no independent FY3/27 forecast at all. For FY3/28, the model's edge over company guidance is +9.1% and its gap to consensus is −5.3%. That is a *narrowing* of the debate, not a differentiated call. **The base case has no meaningful edge over consensus.**

**Where an edge could instead come from — and my assessment:**
- **Timing of Cell 7/Cell 9.** Management intends to decide and disclose within FY3/27 [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026]. This is a genuine, dated catalyst that consensus may not have sized. It is the strongest argument against my Negative rating.
- **Cash-flow quality.** Consensus appears to be valuing earnings, not free cash flow. On my numbers FY3/28 free cash flow is roughly −JPY140bn (net profit [[120.0]] + D&A ~JPY90bn − capex ~JPY350bn). A market that starts pricing negative FCF would derate the stock. This is a risk to the stock, not an edge in my favour relative to consensus.
- **Duration of growth.** Management's own FY3/31 target of JPY300bn+ operating profit is unchanged and excludes three identified expansion projects. If those are added, the terminal earnings power is higher than the model's FY3/29 [[230.0]]. This is real optionality but it is beyond a 3–6 month horizon.

**Evidence that would confirm a more positive view:** a Cell 7/Cell 9 announcement with disclosed customer commitments and a revised FY3/31 target above JPY300bn; Q3 operating profit at or above JPY36.5bn with Electronics margin at or above 30%; evidence that Cell 8 is qualified and loading on schedule.

## 9. Valuation

**Method:** forward P/E on FY3/28 EPS, cross-checked with EV/EBITDA and free-cash-flow yield. P/E is appropriate because the business is profitable and growing; EV/EBITDA is a necessary cross-check because depreciation is about to step up sharply and because the company carries net cash. I do not use DCF: the capex path beyond FY3/29 is not disclosed with enough precision, and a DCF would give false precision to a terminal value that depends on Cell 7/9 decisions not yet made.

**Basis:** price [[JPY 8,045]]; EPS on the model's ~566m share count; net cash of ~JPY258bn; minority interest JPY7.6bn.

| Metric | FY3/27 | FY3/28 | FY3/29 |
|---|---|---|---|
| P/E at [[JPY 8,045]] | [[51.2x]] | 38.0x | 29.8x |
| P/E on fully diluted ~590m shares | ~53.8x | ~39.6x | ~31.0x |
| EV/EBITDA (my calc) | 20.2x | 16.0x | ~12.7x |
| FCF yield (my calc) | ~+0.7% | ~−3.1% | ~−3.1% |
| Dividend yield | 0.25% | — | — |

Market capitalisation is ~JPY4,565bn (567.4m shares × [[JPY 8,045]]); enterprise value ~JPY4,314bn after net cash and minorities.

**Fair value.** The model's band is [[JPY 4,715]]–[[JPY 7,858]] with a base of [[JPY 7,628]] and scenarios of [[JPY 5,085]] (bear, [[−37]]%), [[JPY 7,628]] (base, [[−5]]%) and [[JPY 7,806]] (bull, [[−3]]%). My own cross-check: 30x FY3/28 EPS of [[211.9]] = JPY6,357; 36x = JPY7,628; 40x = JPY8,476. A 30–37x range on FY3/28 earnings gives roughly **JPY6,400–7,900**, consistent with the model's base. I would centre fair value at **JPY7,300–7,600**.

**The critical observation: the current price of [[JPY 8,045]] is above the top of the model's entire fair-value band of [[JPY 7,858]], and above even the bull case of [[JPY 7,806]].** The stock is not discounting the base case; it is discounting something better than the bull case.

**Why 38x FY3/28 is demanding:** the company has negative free cash flow, rising depreciation, a 35%-of-sales capex programme, and a management team that explicitly models price declines. A 38x multiple on a capital-intensive manufacturer is a scarcity premium, and scarcity premiums compress when a third supplier is qualified — which management itself confirms is happening in AI GPUs [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026].

**Sensitivities:**
- Each 1x of FY3/28 P/E is worth ~JPY212 per share.
- A 10% cut to FY3/28 operating profit ([[180.0]] → JPY162bn) with a constant 36x multiple would take fair value to roughly JPY6,900.
- A 5pp higher tax rate or a 10% stronger yen would each take several percent off EPS; the corpus does not permit a precise sensitivity.

**Peer comparison is not possible** — no peer multiples are in the corpus. This is a material limitation on the valuation conclusion: I can say the stock is expensive relative to its own cash generation and relative to the model's fair-value band, but I cannot say it is expensive relative to Shinko, ASE or Unimicron on a like-for-like basis.

## 11. Risks and invalidation conditions

**Business risk**
- **Customer concentration** is undisclosed but clearly high. A single AI accelerator customer's package redesign or dual-sourcing decision would be material.
- **Third-supplier entry.** Management confirms the AI GPU substrate market is shifting from two players to three with a Korean entrant, and that Shinko is winning Tier-2 CPU orders [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026]. Management argues total capacity still falls short of demand; Citi argues the resulting share decline "poses a risk of a temporary stock price correction" [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026]. I weight the multiple-compression risk more heavily than the earnings risk.
- **EMIB-T yield.** Management concedes it is "struggling significantly with yield improvement" [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call]. A public yield failure would hit both the multiple and the FY3/29+ forecast.

**Forecast risk**
- **The H2 FY3/27 step-up is the weakest link.** H2 operating profit of [[72.9]]bn requires +21% HoH and +148% YoY, with Ceramics falling to JPY2.1bn. If Electronics H2 revenue does not grow ~25% HoH, the year misses.
- **The FY3/28 revenue increment of [[95.0]]bn** rests on Cell 8 timing that management has only described as "sequential operation from FY2027" — construction completion, equipment installation, qualification and revenue recognition are not the same event, and the corpus does not distinguish them.

**Balance-sheet and cash-flow risk**
- **Negative free cash flow of roughly −JPY140bn in FY3/28 and FY3/29** consumes the net cash position. Funding depends on customer advances continuing to grow (they grew JPY118.8bn in one half) and on convertible bond conversion. A pause in customer prepayments would force debt issuance or equity.
- **Dilution** from the remaining ~JPY44.5bn of convertible bonds (~20m shares, ~3.4% of shares out).

**Valuation risk**
- 38x FY3/28 earnings with a 0.25% dividend yield and negative FCF leaves no margin of safety. The stock is above the model's entire fair-value band.

**Regulatory / geopolitical risk**
- Not addressed in the corpus. The company operates Japanese and Malaysian plants and sells into US-designed AI accelerators; export controls and US-China technology policy are an unquantified exposure. I flag this as a gap rather than analyse it.

**Thesis invalidation (what would make me wrong)**
- A Cell 7/Cell 9 announcement with disclosed customer commitments plus an FY3/31 target raised materially above JPY300bn, accompanied by Q3 operating profit above JPY36.5bn. That combination would justify a higher multiple and would invalidate the Negative rating.
- Conversely, the Negative rating is confirmed by Q3 operating profit below JPY33bn, Electronics margin below 28%, or a Cell 8 qualification delay.

Treat a standard allocation as one full position (roughly 3% of the portfolio); Underweight means holding about 40–50% of that, i.e. taking a 3% position down to roughly 1.2–1.5% and holding the proceeds in cash or funding the underweight.
